hypotheses.title: Incremental 24-hour volatility forecasting
hypotheses.claim: Funding extremes plus price-dislocation/smoothing features improve out-of-sample forecasts of next-24-hour realized variance of mark-price returns over a realized-volatility-only HAR-style baseline.
hypotheses.estimand: Paired out-of-sample QLIKE difference (C2 vs B1) on the frozen test panel.

prior_tests.result: C2 vs B1: -2.50% relative QLIKE reduction; 95% CI [-0.123401, 0.158843] crosses zero; test window single ~4-day block

C2 vs B1: -9.28% relative QLIKE reduction; 95% CI [-0.097648, -0.008788] does NOT cross zero; n=8274 paired rows across 5 symbols (BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, BNBUSDT, SOLUSDT, XRPUSDT); test window 2024-07-23T00:00:00Z..2024-09-30T23:00:00Z = 70 days = only 2 non-overlapping 30-day blocks
prior_tests.verdict: INCONCLUSIVE; primary contrast numerically met and CI supports improvement, but minimum-claim-worthy test (>=3 non-overlapping 30-day blocks) NOT MET. Independently reproduced 2026-10-28 by re-running frozen scripts/run_evaluation.py with FCLR_EXPERIMENT=FCLR-002 (byte-identical numbers).

hypotheses.next_falsification_test: Pre-registered FCLR-003 (or later) with >=3 non-overlapping 30-day evaluation blocks across >=5 instruments, uncertainty supporting improvement after multiplicity correction, before any risk-overlay phase.
hypotheses.superseded_by: FCLR-002 (numbers independently reproduced 2026-10-28, but frozen test window 2024-07-23..2024-09-30 = 70 days = only 2 non-overlapping 30-day blocks; protocol >=3-block requirement NOT MET. Gate: primary contrast met numerically, minimum-claim-worthy test NOT MET -> INCONCLUSIVE, same as FCLR-001.)

hypotheses.title: Funding-extreme correction-time replication
hypotheses.claim: The working-paper pattern (Shek, SSRN, posted 29 Sep 2026) of shorter median funding-extreme correction times in low-volatility versus high-volatility conditions can be independently reconstructed from admissible public Binance data.
hypotheses.estimand: Median/mean time-to-correction among corrected funding-extreme events, split by realized-volatility regime.
hypotheses.directional_claim: Correction time lower in low-volatility conditions.
hypotheses.status_evidence: scripts/funding_correction_replication.py; tests/test_funding_correction_replication.py (4/4 passed); 445 funding-extreme events across 5 symbols Jan-Mar 2024

prior_tests.result: Median correction time 8.0h, mean 12.6h among corrected events (Jan-Mar 2024, 5 symbols)
prior_tests.verdict: Partial: full paper methodology not independently reconstructible from public sources alone

hypotheses.next_falsification_test: Obtain and document the paper's full event-definition and censoring rules; if unavailable, report as partial replication and do not promote correction-time association to volatility-forecast or liquidation evidence.

hypotheses.title: Hypothetical boundary-breach forecast
hypotheses.claim: Funding and price-dislocation features improve out-of-sample forecasts of whether mark prices breach a precomputed hypothetical long/short liquidation boundary within a pre-specified horizon under disclosed margin/leverage assumptions.
hypotheses.estimand: Brier score / log loss / precision-recall on synthetic mark-price boundary-breach labels.
hypotheses.directional_claim: Candidate models beat the volatility-only baseline on breach probability.
hypotheses.status_evidence: Two pre-registered out-of-sample breach evaluations run; neither supports an incremental-skill claim. research_state/evaluation_summary_h003.md (FCLR-001 block, n=70/scenario, base rate 0.0000 everywhere -> degenerate, no events). research_state/evaluation_summary_h003_FCLR002.md (FCLR-002 block, n=8274-8280/scenario, real events at 5x/10x/20x) -> C2 does not beat B0 on Brier or log-loss in any scenario; AUPRC gains are small and best-F1 thresholds are descriptive only (no pre-specified alert budget passed).

prior_tests.result: 8 leverage/side scenarios, n=70 each, base_rate=0.0000 across all (zero breach events in 2024-03-27..2024-03-30). Brier/log-loss/AUPRC degenerate.

8 leverage/side scenarios on FCLR-002 test block 2024-07-23..2024-09-30. Base rates: lev3 0.0000, lev5 long 0.0036/short 0.0033, lev10 long 0.0169/short 0.0153, lev20 long 0.1249/short 0.1025. C2 vs B0 Brier: lev5 long 0.003615 vs 0.003625, lev5 short 0.003244 vs 0.003240, lev10 long 0.016517 vs 0.016589, lev10 short 0.014613 vs 0.014434 (WORSE), lev20 long 0.107891 vs 0.108023, lev20 short 0.089042 vs 0.088904 (WORSE). Log-loss mirrors Brier. AUPRC small positive deltas but precision at best-F1 stays low (<=0.36).
prior_tests.verdict: INCONCLUSIVE; no incremental skill over volatility-only baseline on any pre-specified metric. Funding/price features do not improve boundary-breach probability forecasts in this panel.

hypotheses.next_falsification_test: None pre-registrable without a new protocol version. Candidate directions (not executed, not pre-registered): longer horizon (72h/168h), lower MMR tiers, or an event-intensity target instead of binary breach -- each requires a fresh pre-registration before outcome inspection. Do not threshold-shop on the reported best-F1.
